title: Prompt Engineering Masters Class
description: A full prompt-engineering apprenticeship: patterns that transfer across Codex, Claude, Perplexity, and creative AI—specs, evaluation, libraries, failure diagnosis, and team standards end to end.

lessons.title: Universal Prompt Anatomy

introduction.text: Across tools, strong prompts share anatomy: goal, context, constraints, examples, and output format. Tool differences matter, but structure travels. This apprenticeship builds a cross-tool prompting system you can teach—not trivia for one chatbot.

questions.question: Cross-tool mastery means:
options: Patterns that transfer with local adaptation
questions.correctAnswer: Patterns that transfer with local adaptation

project.title: Anatomy Cheatsheet
project.description: Design a one-page cheatsheet with the universal prompt blocks and 2 example prompts (coding + writing) showing each block labeled in comments or brackets.

questions.question: Context without a goal tends to produce:
Local adaptation means:
options: Tuning the same pattern to Claude vs Codex vs Perplexity
questions.correctAnswer: Tuning the same pattern to Claude vs Codex vs Perplexity

questions.question: Unsafe output risk is lowered by:

objectives: Explain the main idea of "Universal Prompt Anatomy" without looking at notes
Identify one mistake beginners make on this topic and how to avoid it
Complete a concrete artifact for: Anatomy Cheatsheet
keyTakeaways: Across tools, strong prompts share anatomy: goal, context, constraints, examples, and output format.

lessons.title: Tool-Specific Adaptation

introduction.text: Same anatomy, different accents: Codex wants interfaces and tests; Claude wants long-context contracts; Perplexity wants query precision and citations; creative tools want visual constraints. Learn adapters, not entirely new religions per app.

questions.question: Adapters are:
options: Small modifications of a shared core
questions.correctAnswer: Small modifications of a shared core

lessons.title: Evaluation: Rubrics, Tests, and Blind Spots

introduction.text: If you cannot evaluate, you cannot improve prompts. Build rubrics: correctness, completeness, format compliance, and risk. Use golden examples. Watch for sycophancy and confident wrongness. Evaluation is the difference between tinkering and engineering.

options: It is easy to spot always

lessons.title: Failure Diagnosis and Repair Loops

introduction.text: Diagnose failures by class: missing context, conflicting instructions, underspecified format, wrong tool, or evaluation mismatch. Repair with the smallest change. Keep a failure diary. Pros debug prompts; amateurs just rephrase forever.

questions.question: Wrong-tool failures need:
options: Louder prompts to the same tool
Switching or adapting to a better-fit tool
questions.correctAnswer: Switching or adapting to a better-fit tool

lessons.title: Libraries, Governance, and Team Standards

introduction.text: Ship a prompt library with owners, versioning, and allowed tools. Define review rules for high-risk prompts. Teach onboarding with pattern cards. Governance keeps speed from becoming unmanaged risk—masters prompt engineering is organizational.

project.title: Team Prompt Standard
